title: UAV Panoramic Filming for Rapid Indirect Optical Estimation of Leaf Area Index (LAI)
content: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a fundamental structural metric for characterizing terrestrial ecosystems, quantifying carbon sequestration, and understanding canopy physiological processes. The LAI-2200C Plant Canopy Analyzer provides established multi-angular gap-fraction measurements for indirect optical LAI estimation; however, its ground-based operation can be constrained by terrain accessibility, limited spatial coverage, and sky illumination conditions. This study presents an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based approach that uses the upward-facing 180° fisheye camera of a DJI Avata 360 platform to approximate the hemispherical viewing geometry and multi-angular sampling of the LAI-2200C. The circular fisheye imagery is processed directly by identifying the image centre and calibrating its projection geometry to convert pixel positions into zenith angles. Five concentric angular masks corresponding to the LAI-2200C’s viewing rings are then applied to extract canopy gap fractions from classified sky and vegetation pixels. The resulting multi-angular gap-fraction measurements are used to estimate effective LAI through the Miller integral approach, providing an image-based alternative to conventional optical measurements. Comparisons with ground-based LAI-2200C observations across on-site plots demonstrate strong agreement, while the UAV platform substantially increases sampling efficiency and spatial coverage. In particular, the first-person-view (FPV) flight capability offers considerable flexibility for collecting canopy observations in steep terrain, dense vegetation, and otherwise inaccessible locations where conventional ground-based measurements are difficult or impractical. This approach provides a rapid, flexible, and potentially scalable alternative for LAI assessment.
